sections.heading: C2 — Collision avoidance and emergencies
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Collision avoidance and emergencies

FACT_ID: sec08-R01 | anchor: A75
Follow the vehicle owner's recommended maintenance schedule to reduce mechanical-failure risk. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R02 | anchor: A75
If the brakes actually stop working, the handbook first recommends several rapid pedal pumps, which may restore enough pressure to stop. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R03 | anchor: A75
If pumping failed brakes does not work, use the described parking-brake handle or pedal gradually to avoid locking rear wheels. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R04 | anchor: A75
If parking-brake application during brake failure starts a skid, be ready to release it. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R05 | anchor: A75
If braking cannot be restored, seek a safe place off the roadway to slow and stop, and do not continue driving without functioning brakes. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R06 | anchor: A75
A blowout is rapid tire deflation; a front blowout can pull the vehicle sharply toward that tire. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R07 | anchor: A75
A rear blowout can cause wobbling, shaking and some pull toward the failed tire. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R08 | anchor: A75
After a blowout or sudden flat, hold the wheel firmly and keep the vehicle straight. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R09 | anchor: A75
For a blowout, release the accelerator and slow gradually; let the vehicle slow naturally, using gentle braking only if necessary. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R10 | anchor: A75
After a blowout, avoid stopping on the road if possible; pull to a safe place, activate hazard flashers and arrange tire replacement. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R11 | anchor: A75
If the engine shuts off while moving, hold the wheel firmly; steering may require greater effort but remains possible. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R12 | anchor: A75
After an engine shutdown, select neutral, seek an escape path and use steady braking rather than a hard application to pull off the road. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R13 | anchor: A75
After stopping for engine shutdown, try restarting; if it fails, raise the hood, use hazard flashers and call for help. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R14 | anchor: A75
Accelerator failure may result from a broken spring or a pedal stuck down. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R15 | anchor: A75
For accelerator failure, select neutral and seek an escape path, then steer smoothly and brake gently to leave the roadway. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R16 | anchor: A75
After stopping for accelerator failure, switch off the vehicle and have the pedal repaired before driving again. [A75]
Source: [A75 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0075]

FACT_ID: sec08-R17 | anchor: A76
If wheels leave the pavement, avoid an immediate panic return because excessive steering before slowing can cause a serious crash. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R18 | anchor: A76
For a pavement drop-off, ease the accelerator, avoid hard braking and use gentle brakes while steering straight. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R19 | anchor: A76
The handbook recommends slowing to 25 mph or less before its pavement-return maneuver. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R20 | anchor: A76
Straddling the pavement edge can keep the tires' inside edges from rubbing and allow a better angle for returning. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R21 | anchor: A76
With traffic gaps in all directions, the described pavement return uses about a quarter-turn of the wheel; avoid oversteering and guide back into the lane after reaching pavement. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R22 | anchor: A76
If traffic is heavy and the shoulder is wide, move fully onto the shoulder and stop, then wait for a large gap before reentering. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R23 | anchor: A76
If returning to pavement is not possible, stop as far from the road as possible and wait for help. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R24 | anchor: A76
A sideways-sliding vehicle can trip over a curb, guardrail, stump or soft uneven ground and roll over. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R25 | anchor: A76
Excess speed or a sharp steering input can contribute to a rollover. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R26 | anchor: A76
A multivehicle impact can also initiate a rollover through lost control or a side strike. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R27 | anchor: A76
SUVs, vans, pickups and small trucks are more rollover-prone than passenger cars because of higher centers of gravity. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R28 | anchor: A76
Additional passengers or cargo can increase rollover risk. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R29 | anchor: A76
Appropriate speed and added caution in bad weather can reduce rollover risk by leaving more response time. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R30 | anchor: A76
Avoid abrupt steering at high speed or on soft surfaces; after leaving pavement, slow gradually instead of jerking back onto it. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R31 | anchor: A76
Seat belts reduce rollover injury and ejection risk by keeping occupants in the vehicle. [A76]
Source: [A76 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0076]

FACT_ID: sec08-R32 | anchor: A77
Rollover-sensing side airbags can help reduce upper-body ground contact and occupant ejection. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R33 | anchor: A77
At night, choose a speed that permits stopping within the distance illuminated and visible ahead. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R34 | anchor: A77
For night driving, the handbook recommends adding at least one second to following space, or at least two seconds on unfamiliar roads at night. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R35 | anchor: A77
When rain, snow, dust, smoke or dense fog limits the forward view to 100 feet, the handbook warns that speeds above 30 mph are unsafe. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R36 | anchor: A77
If adverse weather leaves too little visibility for driving, leave the roadway at a safe place and wait for it to clear. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R37 | anchor: A77
Use low beams and fog lights in fog, snow or heavy rain, including daylight, and watch for unlit vehicles. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R38 | anchor: A77
Sunglasses, clean windows and sun visors can reduce glare from a low sun ahead. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R39 | anchor: A77
With the sun behind the vehicle, opposing drivers may have difficulty seeing it or its turn signals. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R40 | anchor: A77
Slow or adjust position near a hill or curve with a hidden path so there is room to respond to an unseen obstruction. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R41 | anchor: A77
Parked vehicles can hide people or obstruct the view; give them as much clearance as the lane permits. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0077]

FACT_ID: sec08-R42 | anchor: A77
Match speed and position to the visible stopping space, particularly around congestion, hills, curves and weather restrictions. [A77]
Source: [A77 -> src:rdmv-ks-c:kansas-department-of-revenue-division-of:handbook:pdf-0077]

Misconceptions: ABS hard-stop technique differs from non-ABS lockup recovery and from actual brake failure. A tire blowout calls for gradual slowing; visibility advice does not guarantee a speed is safe.
Mnemonics: Editorial cue: identify the failure, preserve control, find space, stop safely. It adds no equipment instruction.
Glossary: Separate front traction loss, rear traction loss, brake failure, tire blowout, engine shutdown, accelerator failure and pavement drop-off using their source-bound conditions.
Dynamic facts: Vehicle controls, airbags and traction systems depend on equipment documentation; numerical risk and stopping claims with missing assumptions remain typed debt. The edition's procedures require issuer refresh before replacing this source.

ranked.label: Coverage of Collision avoidance and emergencies; pedagogic emphasis only, no official exam weights asserted

corpus_stability.reason: The bound Kansas handbook has one February 2022 revision label; the selected source contains no evidence of multiple annual corpus rewrites. Later legal or administrative changes require issuer rechecking.

market_signal.origin_note: Market evidence is handled in part E.
